strongest_angle: Examination of the Tennessee Valley Authority's Unit 2 rebuild at Fort Loudoun Dam where an Office of Inspector General report revealed that 196 out of 240 welds failed inspection, driving total project costs to $55.8 million against an original $27.4 million authorization.

key_facts.fact: The Tennessee Valley Authority Office of Inspector General released a November 4 report detailing that 196 of 240 welds on the discharge ring at Fort Loudoun Dam failed inspection.
The Unit 2 rebuild project at Fort Loudoun Dam near Lenoir City, Tennessee, cost $55.8 million, which was more than double its original $27.4 million authorization.
A new 375,000-pound turbine was installed at Fort Loudoun Dam to replace one that ran for more than 80 years, according to an Office of Inspector General report released on November 4.
The life extension project for Fort Loudoun Hydro Unit 2 was originally initiated in November 2017 to extend the service life of the unit for the next 40 years.
